lessons: Avoid starting with descriptive filler lines (e.g., 'When maple trees wake up...'), which caused a massive 38.5% drop on 'Why Maple Syrup Takes 40 Gallons'.
Do not use rhetorical pauses like 'Pause and guess...', which triggered a 15.4% drop right after the midpoint.
Hook lines that directly challenge viewer intuition (e.g., the spicy food water myth) help sustain above-average end retention (0.56 vs similar) despite a rough start.
Not enough data to definitively rank hook types for 10% retention, as all tested videos suffered from below-average start performance compared to similar YouTube shorts (0.27 to 0.46).
worst_moment_types: Descriptive explanatory statements early in the video (around 13% progress)
Direct pauses and guessing prompts (around 52% progress)
best_hook_types: Contrasting myth-busting statements that address common everyday habits
